title: Workspace Control Plane v2
goal: Design, implement, and validate a workspace-control v2 architecture that generalizes the proven tutor, Codex, DIRECT_TOOL, human-gate, and PADataset/MILCOM workflow evidence into an executor-neutral, resumable multi-stage control plane without moving project-domain authority out of project repositories.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed v2 architecture specification defines owner, workflow, stage, task execution, reasoning executor, operation surface, execution topology, checkpoint, artifact class, validation barrier, resumability, HANDOFF_SAFE semantics, executor/surface selection, workspace-control ownership, and project-local ownership.
The shared operator/tutor bridge concepts and proven Codex adapter concepts are deliberately integrated rather than blindly merged, while executor-specific adapters remain thin.
Portability is generalized beyond a two-party Codex versus ChatGPT+human model to distinguish reasoning executor, operation surface, topology/data locality, authority, and consequence.
Reusable project-owned workflow descriptors are distinguished from live task capsules; workflow descriptors define stable procedure while capsules define one execution's durable progress.
Coordination supports remote-only, local, and composed/hybrid execution topologies without manufacturing local state solely to legitimize remote DIRECT_TOOL work.

Task execution is stage-oriented: material stages have preconditions, bounded authority, expected outputs, validation, durable identities when required, stop/failure conditions, and resumable progress.
Artifact lifecycle/Git policy and safe deterministic worktree preparation are represented without making workspace-control own project-specific artifact semantics.

Regression validation covers DIRECT_TOOL-only work, DIRECT_TOOL to local runtime transitions, human-gate suspension/resume, ChatGPT to Codex and Codex to ChatGPT handoff, remote-only handoff, local-runtime handoff, and ambiguous-failure recovery before promotion to main.
constraints: Do not modify PADataset during the v2 architecture/refactor until the new control plane is validated and an explicit later migration consumes it.
Do not modify MTH602, EAS501, CIS560, or other course repositories merely to implement workspace-control v2.
Preserve phase4-codex-adapters at 9d2c088e1929a6a1cdc2aaca6ec1393c3e1e6859 and phase4-chatgpt-to-codex-handoff at 726c31f855d723943cc24b8d31448cf5eaa5532e as evidence; do not redo Phase 4C.
Preserve shared-operator-tutor-contract at 450eebeef6b76a674913949863082277b6bdb811 as the provisional tutor/operator evidence branch until deliberate integration.
Project/domain authority remains inside the owning project repository; workspace-control owns reusable coordination, portability, routing, and execution semantics only.

Do not make LangGraph, Temporal, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, GitOps tooling, or another framework the canonical control plane; use external systems only as design references unless separately justified.
Do not create a large permanent executor-capability database before the minimal v2 selection/validation requirements are clear.
Do not blindly retry failed or ambiguous mutations; inspect actual durable state first.
For the first implementation phase, mutate only the v2 architecture specification path on the refactor branch; expand mutation scope only after that specification is reviewed.
decisions: Use a separate coordination branch for the task capsule and a separate refactor branch for actual v2 mutations, following the pattern proven in Phase 4C.
Treat project-local domain authority, shared behavioral contracts, workspace coordination/durable task state, thin executor adapters, and actual executors/surfaces as separate architectural layers.
Treat DIRECT_TOOL as a first-class autonomous surface for operation classes that have empirical evidence, but keep trust operation-class specific.
Distinguish reasoning executor from operation surface and from execution topology/data locality; do not encode current GitHub-versus-terminal limitations as permanent executor assignments.
Treat HUMAN_BROWSER_INGRESS, HUMAN_TERMINAL, specialized external-tool execution, and substantive human judgment as different kinds of boundaries.
Keep artifact completion separate from student mastery; this remains a tutoring-contract invariant rather than a generic control-plane state.
Adopt the principle 'more verified stages per autonomous control cycle' rather than optimizing merely for fewer messages.
Introduce reusable project-owned workflow descriptors as a v2 design target, distinct from live task capsules.
Introduce stage-level validation and resumability as v2 design targets so completed stages are not replayed after suspension or partial failure.

Use MILCOM/PADataset evidence to evaluate named deterministic project entrypoints, artifact lifecycle declarations, safe worktree preparation, and project-owned cross-authority consistency validators.
Use external systems such as Anthropic workflow/agent guidance, Temporal, LangGraph, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, GitOps, and asset-oriented orchestration only as comparative design references.

notes: Empirical evidence feeding v2 includes: MTH602 tutoring/persistence/completion-vs-mastery; EAS501 empty-repo DIRECT_TOOL bootstrap, browser-ingress boundary, cold-start tutoring and inline persistence/return routing; CIS560 typed-authority and composed-workflow experimental design; MILCOM/PADataset remote Git -> local runtime -> artifact QA workflow; and Phase-4 Codex durable task handoff/recovery. External architectural references include workflow-vs-agent guidance, durable execution, graph orchestration, guardrails/tracing, GitOps-style versioned authority, and asset-oriented orchestration. These are design references, not canonical dependencies.
